subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw preserve the existing effective one-at-a-time same-session `ContextEngine.maintain()` behavior after a timeout, or intentionally introduce a new re-entrant plugin contract?
rationale: The PR currently makes installed plugins responsible for a new concurrency condition that the host cannot fully fence. Choosing an invocation tail/coalescing design versus an additive abort-capable SDK contract is a public plugin-boundary decision.

options.title: Preserve serialization
options.body: Keep the timeout and host fence, but prevent a later same-session maintenance invocation from entering a plugin until the timed-out invocation settles; coalesce intervening work as needed.

options.title: Design an additive cancellation contract
options.body: Define and document an explicit abort/cancellation lifecycle for `maintain()` first, then use it to request cooperative shutdown before allowing another invocation.

options.title: Accept re-entrancy
options.body: Land the documented concurrent-maintenance requirement and explicitly accept that existing context-engine plugins must adapt their own synchronization.

recommendation.title: Preserve serialization
recommendation.body: Keep the timeout and host fence, but prevent a later same-session maintenance invocation from entering a plugin until the timed-out invocation settles; coalesce intervening work as needed.
